_doc: Hook-up wire by American Wire Gauge: the copper's area from the gauge's definition, and how much current a wire in a machine should be asked to carry. The current density is a working limit for short runs in free air and is an estimate: feel the wire under load.
name: wire

current_density.rule: Current a hook-up wire in a machine may carry per square millimetre of copper, for short runs in free air: under the 17 A/mm² chassis-wiring figure, as wires in a bundle or a chain run warmer
current_density.source: PowerStream's AWG chart gives 2.2 A for 26 AWG (0.128 mm², 17 A/mm²) as chassis wiring, https://www.powerstream.com/Wire_Size.htm; taken at about 0.6 of it

service_loop.rule: Slack added to a wire's longest run, for a strain relief and the connector
service_loop.source: A working allowance; the wire's route is otherwise taken as drawn

signal_current.rule: What a signal wire (an endstop, a step line) carries
signal_current.source: Arduino Uno I/O pins are rated 20 mA, https://docs.arduino.cc/hardware/uno-rev3/

awg_base.rule: A wire of gauge n is 0.127 × 92^((36 − n) / 39) mm across
